violations.description: Real credentials committed and persisted in git history (config/credentials.json)
violations.evidence: scan_secrets identified hardcoded_credential in config/credentials.json added in commit 6e0b40e and deleted in commit 45b2b4e
violations.recommendation: Rewrite git history using git-filter-repo or BFG Repo-Cleaner to purge historical credentials and rotate all leaked secrets.

violations.description: Secret-bearing .env file committed to version control with production database credentials and secret key
violations.evidence: .env contains environment variables with real credentials (lines 2-3)
violations.recommendation: Remove .env from version control, add .env to .gitignore, rotate compromised credentials, and use environment variables or secret management.

violations.description: Dangerous pull_request_target workflow executing untrusted PR code with repo privileges
violations.evidence: .github/workflows/deploy.yml triggers on pull_request_target and checks out PR head sha (lines 5, 21)
violations.recommendation: Use standard pull_request trigger or avoid checking out and executing untrusted PR code in privileged workflows.

violations.description: Secret printed to CI logs via echo command
violations.evidence: .github/workflows/deploy.yml prints registry token to stdout via echo "Using token ${{ secrets.REGISTRY_TOKEN }}" (line 25)
violations.recommendation: Remove print statements that expose secrets and rely on silent CLI authentication (e.g. --password-stdin).

violations.description: Hardcoded AWS access key ID and database password in source configuration
violations.evidence: app/config.py contains hardcoded AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID and DB_PASSWORD (lines 8, 15)
violations.recommendation: Load credentials from environment variables using os.environ instead of hardcoding them in source code.

violations.description: Risky deployment automation running on every push without a test validation gate
violations.evidence: .github/workflows/deploy.yml triggers on push without requiring passing test jobs (line 4)
violations.recommendation: Require successful test workflow completion before allowing deployment jobs to run.

violations.description: Incorrect CI trigger branch filter (configured for 'master' while repository default branch is 'main')
violations.evidence: .github/workflows/ci.yml triggers on push to branches: [master] (line 5)
violations.recommendation: Update branch filters to include 'main' or remove branch restriction to run on default branch pushes.

violations.description: Over-privileged workflow token with write-all permissions
violations.evidence: .github/workflows/ci.yml sets permissions: write-all at top level (line 8)
violations.recommendation: Apply principle of least privilege by setting explicit minimum required permissions (e.g. contents: read).

violations.description: Script injection vulnerability via untrusted github.event data interpolated into run shell commands
violations.evidence: .github/workflows/ci.yml interpolates github.event.pull_request.title directly into bash run command (line 26)
violations.recommendation: Pass untrusted event data via environment variables instead of direct shell interpolation.

violations.description: TLS verification disabled in HTTP client request (verify=False)
violations.evidence: app/storage.py calls requests.get with verify=False (line 27)
violations.recommendation: Enable TLS certificate verification (verify=True or provide CA bundle) to prevent man-in-the-middle attacks.

violations.description: Insecure execution pattern piping remote script directly into bash (curl | sh)
violations.evidence: scripts/deploy.sh executes curl -fsSL https://get.example-deploy-tool.io/install.sh | bash (line 5)
violations.recommendation: Inspect, pin, or securely install deployment tools rather than piping remote scripts directly to bash.

violations.description: Test failures masked in CI using || true
violations.evidence: .github/workflows/ci.yml runs pytest || true which hides test failures (line 29)
violations.recommendation: Remove || true so that test failures correctly fail the CI pipeline gate.

violations.description: Tests that cannot pass because they import a non-existent module
violations.evidence: tests/test_storage.py imports from app.legacy_cache which does not exist in the codebase (line 3)
violations.recommendation: Implement the missing module or remove the obsolete test import.

violations.description: Dockerfile uses latest base image, runs as root, and lacks .dockerignore while copying entire repository context
violations.evidence: Dockerfile uses FROM python:latest and lacks a .dockerignore file (lines 1, 4)
violations.recommendation: Pin base image to specific version (e.g. python:3.12-slim), run as a non-root user, and add a .dockerignore file.

violations.description: GitHub Action referenced by mutable branch reference instead of immutable commit hash or tagged version
violations.evidence: .github/workflows/ci.yml uses codecov/codecov-action@master (line 32)
violations.recommendation: Pin actions to specific immutable commit hashes or pinned semver tags (e.g. @v4).

violations.description: Obvious maintainability problem with bare except clause swallowing all errors
violations.evidence: app/storage.py uses a bare except: pass block (line 30)
violations.recommendation: Catch specific exceptions (e.g. requests.RequestException) rather than a bare except.

violations.description: Committed local/IDE personal settings (.vscode/settings.json)
violations.evidence: .vscode/settings.json is tracked in git and contains local user paths (lines 1-5)
violations.recommendation: Add .vscode/ to .gitignore and remove it from repository tracking.

violations.description: Machine-specific absolute path hardcoded in configuration and IDE settings
violations.evidence: app/config.py defines UPLOAD_DIR with a Windows absolute path C:\Users\ibrahim\... (line 19)
violations.recommendation: Use relative paths or environment-configurable path variables instead of hardcoded local user absolute paths.

violations.description: Inconsistent and conflicting package specifications across requirements.txt and pyproject.toml
violations.evidence: requirements.txt specifies requests>=2.31 and unpinned flask, whereas pyproject.toml specifies requests==2.25.1 and flask==3.0.3 (requirements.txt line 1)
violations.recommendation: Consolidate dependencies into a single manifest (pyproject.toml or requirements.txt) with consistent version constraints.

violations.description: .gitignore is incomplete and fails to exclude common generated files, virtualenvs, logs, and secret files
violations.evidence: .gitignore only lists *.tmp and node_modules/ (lines 1-2)
violations.recommendation: Update .gitignore to exclude Python bytecode (__pycache__, *.pyc), logs/, .env, and .vscode/.

violations.description: Generated/temporary files tracked in git (Python bytecode and application log file)
violations.evidence: app/__pycache__/storage.cpython-312.pyc and logs/app.log are tracked in version control
violations.recommendation: Remove logs/, bytecode caches, and build artifacts from git history and tracking.
